This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user requested building a complete invoicing system incrementally, establishing four house rules upfront: (1) money always as integer cents using roundCents() for fractions, (2) never throw for bad input—return fail(CODE) and add to ERRORS, (3) never mutate arguments—return new objects/arrays, (4) run npm test before completion. Features were requested sequentially with a consistent pattern: "Feature Name. Add [function](signature) in [file]. It [description]. Errors: [list]. Add tests." The system grew from basic invoice creation to a comprehensive platform with 22+ features including multi-currency support, bulk discounts, late fees, CSV export, customer deduplication, and dashboard metrics. The final request (current) is: "Polish renderInvoiceText. Keep what it shows today and add each line's discount (for lines that have one), the voucher (if any) just before the total, then a 'Due: ' line with the due date when the invoice has one, and a 'Paid: ' line with the amount paid so far when it has payments. Add tests."

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Result pattern: ok() and fail() returns instead of exceptions
   - Customer tier-based automatic discounts (gold 5%, silver 2.5%, standard 0%)
   - Per-line VAT calculation with rounding on post-discount amount, then summed
   - UTC-only date arithmetic via custom dates.js module
   - Bulk discount: 2.5% extra discount for lines with qty >= 10, applied after regular discount
   - Customer ID normalization (trim + uppercase)
   - Separate numbering schemes: invoices (INV-YYYY-NNNN) and credit notes (CN-YYYY-NNNN)
   - Status progression: draft → issued → paid/partially_paid
   - Payment terms: NET14 (14 days), NET30 (30 days), EOM (end of month)
   - Line enrichment: SKU input expanded to include name, unitPrice, vatRate from catalogue
   - Immutable data: all operations return new copies
   - Foreign currency support with exchange rates: EUR 1.0, USD 1.085, GBP 0.8425
   - Late fees: 0.04% daily on overdue amount
   - CSV formatting with proper escaping (quotes around fields with commas/quotes)

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - src/invoices.js: Main invoice management; exports createInvoice, issueInvoice, addLine, removeLine, applyVoucher, and re-exports lineTotal, lineDiscount, lineVat, invoiceTotals from totals.js
   - src/totals.js: Calculation logic moved for modularity; exports lineTotal (qty * unitPrice), lineDiscount (includes bulk discount when qty >= 10), lineVat (VAT on discounted base), invoiceTotals (returns {subtotal, discount, vat, voucher, total})
   - src/customers.js: Customer lookup and merging; exports normalizeId, getCustomer, validateCustomer, mergeCustomers, TIER_DISCOUNTS; mergeCustomers removes duplicate customer and reassigns all invoices to target customer
   - src/money.js: RATES export {EUR: 1, USD: 1.085, GBP: 0.8425}, convert(cents, currency), formatMoney(cents, currency); roundCents function with half-to-even rounding
   - src/dates.js: isValidDate (validates YYYY-MM-DD), addDays, daysBetween, lastDayOfMonth (all UTC-only)
   - src/catalogue.js: Product data with SKU, name, unitPrice (in cents), vatRate; products include LOGO-PACK (120000¢, 21% VAT), DES-HOUR (8500¢, 21%), STICKER (50¢, 21%), TALK (35000¢, 0% VAT), etc.
   - src/payments.js: recordPayment (adds payment to issued/partially_paid, updates status), balanceDue (total - sum of payments)
   - src/credits.js: createCreditNote (refund record for issued/partially_paid/paid invoices, numbered CN-YYYY-NNNN)
   - src/numbering.js: nextInvoiceNumber (INV-YYYY-NNNN format), separate counter per year
   - src/export.js: exportCsv (returns CSV string with header and rows, formats amounts as euros with 2 decimals and dot separator, escapes fields with commas/quotes)
   - src/reports.js: overdueInvoices (filters to issued/partially_paid with dueDate < asOf, returns {number, customerId, dueDate, daysOverdue, due}), vatSummary (groups lines by VAT rate, returns {rate, base, vat}), lateFee (0.04% per day on due amount for overdue invoices), dashboard (returns {counts by status, outstanding, overdue: {count, amount}, topCustomers: top 3 by due})
   - src/render.js: renderInvoiceText (renders invoice as plain text with customer name, line items with qty/name/unitPrice/lineTotal); needs enhancement to show line discounts, voucher, due date, paid amount
   - src/statements.js: statement (filtered/sorted invoices for customer with {number, issueDate, dueDate, total, due})

4. Errors and fixes:
   - Test data SKU errors: Tests referenced non-existent SKUs (LOGO-A, IDENTITY-B) → fixed by using actual catalogue SKUs (LOGO-PACK, DES-HOUR, etc.)
   - VAT rate mismatches: Test expected BRAND-BOOK to have 9% VAT but catalogue has 21% → corrected all VAT calculation test expectations to 21%
   - Tier discount confusion: Tests didn't account for automatic tier discount application to invoices without explicit discountPercent → updated tests to expect tier discounts
   - issueInvoice field preservation: Function initially didn't preserve terms/dueDate from draft → added: `terms: invoice.terms, dueDate: invoice.dueDate` and conditionally spread voucher/payments
   - Overdue report empty results: Tests failed with dueDate not preserved → fixed by ensuring issueInvoice includes `dueDate: invoice.dueDate`
   - Invalid payment terms in tests: Tests used NET7 which is not valid (only NET14, NET30, EOM allowed) → corrected all test terms to valid values
   - Bulk discount test calculation errors: Test expectations didn't account for 2.5% bulk discount on qty >= 10 → recalculated all affected test assertions with bulk discount impact
   - CSV export rounding errors: Tests expected amounts that didn't match actual rounded calculations → updated test expectations to match half-to-even rounding results
   - Totals.js refactoring import errors: When lineDiscount was moved to totals.js and bulk discount added, invoices.js needed to import and re-export for backward compatibility → added re-exports to maintain API
   - Exchange rate calculation precision: Tests had wrong expected values for currency conversion → recalculated using exact RATES values and roundCents rounding

5. Problem Solving:
   - Immutability: Consistently used spread operators and map() to create new objects/arrays rather than mutating inputs; tests verified this with JSON.stringify before/after comparisons
   - Rounding precision: Implemented half-to-even banker's rounding via roundCents function to handle edge cases; used consistently across money calculations, VAT, discounts
   - Date handling: Avoided timezone bugs by creating UTC-only date functions rather than using JavaScript's default timezone-aware Date object
   - Backward compatibility during refactoring: When moving calculation functions to totals.js, preserved access through re-exports in invoices.js so existing imports continue to work
   - Error handling: Consistently used fail(CODE) pattern for all error cases, maintaining error codes in errors.js export
   - Test coverage: Added 12-30 tests per feature covering happy paths, all error codes, boundary conditions, and immutability verification

6. All user messages:
   - "Establish house rules: (1) money always integer cents using roundCents() for fractions, (2) never throw for bad input—return fail(CODE) and add to ERRORS, (3) never mutate arguments—return new objects/arrays, (4) run npm test before completion. Build invoicing system with 16 features incrementally."
   - "Feature 1: Invoice creation. Add createInvoice({customerId, issueDate, lines, terms}) to src/invoices.js. It creates draft invoices, enriches lines from catalogue with name/unitPrice/vatRate, applies tier discounts, calculates dueDate from terms (NET14/NET30/EOM). Errors: CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND, DATE_INVALID, TERMS_INVALID, NO_LINES, QTY_INVALID, DISCOUNT_INVALID, UNKNOWN_SKU. Add tests."
   - [14 similar feature requests following the same pattern through feature 16]
   - "Refactor: src/invoices.js has grown too big. Move lineTotal, invoiceTotals and the helpers they use into a new src/totals.js. Everything that can be imported from src/invoices.js today must still be importable from there and behave the same. Add tests for src/totals.js."
   - "Bulk discount. A line with 10 or more units gets an extra 2.5% off, applied after the line's own (or tier) discount to what is left. invoiceTotals counts it in discount, and VAT is on what remains. Add tests."
   - "Dashboard. Add dashboard(invoices, asOf) to src/reports.js. It returns { counts, outstanding, overdue, topCustomers }: counts has the number of invoices per status (draft, issued, partially_paid, paid), outstanding is the total still due on the invoices with status 'issued' or 'partially_paid', overdue is { count, amount } from overdueInvoices, and topCustomers are the 3 customers with the most still due, as [{ customerId, due }], highest first. Add tests."
   - "Last request: polish renderInvoiceText. Keep what it shows today and add each line's discount (for lines that have one), the voucher (if any) just before the total, then a 'Due: ' line with the due date when the invoice has one, and a 'Paid: ' line with the amount paid so far when it has payments. Add tests. CRITICAL: Respond with TEXT ONLY. Do NOT call any tools."

7. Pending Tasks:
   - Polish renderInvoiceText function to add:
     - Display line discounts for lines that have them
     - Display voucher amount just before total line (if voucher exists)
     - Display "Due: " line with due date (if invoice has dueDate)
     - Display "Paid: " line with total amount paid so far (if invoice has payments)
   - Add comprehensive tests for the enhanced renderInvoiceText

8. Current Work:
   The system had 367 passing tests covering 22 features including invoice management, multi-currency support, bulk discounts, late fees, CSV export, customer merging, and dashboard reporting. The most recent implementation was the dashboard function which aggregates invoice metrics including counts by status, outstanding amounts, overdue statistics, and top 3 customers by due amount. All features follow the house rules: money as integer cents, fail() pattern for errors, immutability, and comprehensive test coverage. The codebase now includes modular functions with clear separation of concerns after the refactoring that moved calculation logic to totals.js.

9. Optional Next Step:
   Implement the polish to renderInvoiceText function. Current rendering shows customer name and line items with qty/name/unitPrice/lineTotal. The enhancement needs to:
   1. Display discounts on each line that has a discount (discountPercent > 0) — show the discount amount in euros
   2. Add a voucher line before the total (if invoice.voucher exists) — format as "Voucher: -€X.XX"
   3. Add a "Due: " line with the due date when invoice has dueDate field
   4. Add a "Paid: " line with total amount paid when invoice has payments — sum all payment amounts
   Create tests verifying: line discount display, voucher display, due date display, paid amount display, and combinations of these. The user explicitly requested NO tool use in the response.

- Due date displays for issued invoices (e.g., "Due: 2026-10-21"), but not for draft invoices
- Paid amount displays when there are payments (e.g., "Paid: €500.00"), summing all payment amounts

- Line discount display verification
- Voucher display before total
- Due date display for issued invoices
